title: EKG Axis Interpreter
sources: Cadogan M, Buttner R. ECG Axis Interpretation. Life in the Fast Lane (LITFL), updated Nov 2024. https://litfl.com/ecg-axis-interpretation/ (adult bands, methods, differentials, birth axis range)
LITFL. Paediatric ECG: stepwise approach. https://litfl.com/paediatric-ecg-stepwise-approach/ (pediatric normal ranges by age; northwest axis at birth)

Surawicz B, et al. AHA/ACCF/HRS recommendations for the standardization and interpretation of the electrocardiogram, Part III: intraventricular conduction disturbances. J Am Coll Cardiol. 2009;53(11):976-981. doi:10.1016/j.jacc.2008.12.013 (LAFB and LPFB criteria)

Aro AL, Huikuri HV, Tikkanen JT, et al. QRS-T angle as a predictor of sudden cardiac death in a middle-aged general population. Europace. 2012;14(6):872-876 (QRS-T angle ≥100° and arrhythmic death, driven mainly by abnormal T axis)

Walsh JA 3rd, et al. Prognostic value of frontal QRS-T angle in patients without clinical evidence of cardiovascular disease (from the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis). Am J Cardiol. 2013;112:1880-1884 (approximate QRS-T angle bands)

Otake S, et al. Clinical utility of the electrocardiographic P-wave axis in patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. Respiration. 2022;101(4):345-352 (P axis >75° definition and COPD association)

changelog.change: Initial entry. Five input modes — machine P-R-T axes (default), quadrant, 3-lead, isoelectric lead, and precise amplitudes — with adult and age-banded pediatric normals, a QRS-T angle, lead-reversal detection, fascicular-block checklists, and differentials. Engine parity-tested on web and iOS against 46 shared golden vectors.

purpose: P-R-T axes, QRS axis deviation, QRS-T angle. Paste the machine's P-R-T axes, or work the axis out from lead polarities or amplitudes.

modes.label: Machine (P-R-T)
modes.help: Enter the axes from the machine read in the order printed: P, QRS, T. Paste the whole header line if easier. Leave P blank if the machine printed *** or nothing (AF, flutter, junctional).

modes.label: Quadrant (I, aVF)
modes.help: Is the QRS mostly positive, negative, or equiphasic in each lead? Fastest estimate; I+/aVF− needs lead II to separate normal from LAD.

modes.label: 3-Lead (I, II, aVF)
modes.help: Adding lead II separates physiologic from pathologic left axis.

modes.label: Isoelectric lead
modes.help: Tap the most equiphasic limb lead, then mark at least one other lead positive or negative. Axis is 90° from the isoelectric lead, toward the positive leads.

modes.label: Precise (amplitudes)
modes.help: Enter net QRS amplitude (R minus the larger of Q or S, in mm) for any two or more limb leads. Leads I and II are the most reliable pair.

vertical.label: Vertical P axis (>+75°)
vertical.detail: Associated with emphysema/COPD, and with more severe airflow limitation in COPD.

superior.label: Superior P axis (<0°)
superior.detail: P negative in the inferior leads: low/ectopic atrial rhythm or retrograde P (junctional).

negative_lead_I.label: P negative in lead I (beyond ±90°)
negative_lead_I.detail: Consider LA/RA limb lead reversal, dextrocardia, or a left atrial ectopic rhythm.

absent.label: No P axis reported
absent.detail: Check the rhythm: AF, flutter, junctional, or artifact.

outside_reference.label: T axis outside 0° to +90°
outside_reference.detail: Interpret through the QRS-T angle below.

abnormal.label: QRS-T angle wide (>90°)
abnormal.detail: Wide frontal QRS-T angle is associated with higher cardiac and all-cause mortality. Cutoffs are approximate; true normal limits differ by sex.

secondary_repolarization.label: QRS-T angle not interpretable
secondary_repolarization.detail: BBB, pacing, LVH, WPW, or wide QRS produce secondary repolarization changes; prognostic cutoffs were not validated in these patients.

limb_lead_reversal_vs_dextrocardia.text: P and QRS both negative in lead I. Rule out LA/RA limb lead reversal before calling RAD. Check precordial R-wave progression: normal suggests lead reversal; reversed progression suggests dextrocardia.

qrs_t_angle_high_risk.text: QRS-T angle ≥100° has been associated with arrhythmic death in a general-population cohort, driven mainly by an abnormal T axis. Correlate with prior ECGs and clinical context.

lafb_checklist.text: Axis −45° to −90°: check for left anterior fascicular block.

lpfb_checklist.text: Right axis deviation: LPFB is a diagnosis of exclusion. Rule out RVH, lateral MI, PE, and lead reversal first.

infant_superior_axis.text: Superior (northwest) axis in an infant suggests AV canal defect or ostium primum ASD.

paced_axis_caveat.text: Paced QRS axis reflects the pacing site, not native conduction. Axis categories apply loosely.

check_rhythm_no_p.text: No P axis: confirm the rhythm before interpreting anything else.

warnings.p_assumed_absent: Only two values found after “axes”; read as QRS and T with no P axis. Confirm against the printout.
warnings.add_lead_II: Lead I positive with aVF negative can be normal or LAD. Add lead II: positive = normal, negative = LAD.
warnings.add_leads_or_use_precise: The possible range crosses a category boundary. Add another lead or switch to Precise.
warnings.einthoven_mismatch: Lead I + lead III should equal lead II. These values are off by more than 1 mm; recheck measurements or lead placement.
warnings.goldberger_mismatch: aVR + aVL + aVF should sum to zero. These values are off by more than 1 mm; recheck measurements.

statusMessages.inconsistent: No axis fits these polarities. Recheck each lead, or suspect lead misplacement.
statusMessages.ambiguous: Two possible axes. Mark at least one more lead positive or negative.
statusMessages.indeterminate: Net amplitudes are near zero in every lead: indeterminate axis.
statusMessages.need_two_leads: Enter amplitudes for at least two limb leads.

errors.empty: Enter or paste the axis values.
errors.unparseable: Couldn’t find three axis values. Try the format “54 −42 38”.
errors.out_of_range: Axis values must be between −360° and +360°.

lafb.title: Left anterior fascicular block (AHA/ACCF/HRS 2009)
lafb.caveat: Does not apply to congenital heart disease with left axis present from infancy.

lpfb.title: Left posterior fascicular block (AHA/ACCF/HRS 2009)
items: rS pattern in I and aVL
qR pattern in III and aVF
lpfb.caveat: In children, apply only when a distinct rightward shift from a prior ECG is documented.

lad: Left anterior fascicular block (diagnosis of exclusion)
rad: Left posterior fascicular block (diagnosis of exclusion)
extreme: Ventricular rhythm: VT, AIVR, ventricular ectopy

peds.note: Rightward axis is normal at birth (RV dominance) and moves leftward with age.

toolContent.clinicalTakeaway: Axis is a clue, not a diagnosis. A new shift compared with a prior ECG matters more than the absolute number. Before acting on right or extreme axis, rule out limb lead reversal. A wide QRS-T angle in a narrow-complex, unpaced ECG is a risk marker worth noting.
toolContent.whyThisMatters: Axis deviation narrows the differential fast: fascicular blocks, RV strain, hyperkalemia, sodium-channel toxicity, and ventricular rhythms all declare themselves here. The P and T axes the machine already prints add lead-reversal detection and repolarization risk for free.

buildNote: Code-backed tool (engine: builtin, tool: ekg-axis). The axis math lives in web/src/lib/axisEngine.js and ios/Sources/Calc/AxisEngine.swift; both run tools/fixtures/axis-golden-vectors.json. Never compute the axis as atan2(aVF, I): augmented leads read √3/2 of the true projection, so the engine solves by least squares. The hexaxial wheel is an original drawing; LITFL figures are CC BY-NC-SA and are not reproduced. The interpretation bands above are the adult reference, shown for completeness — the tool applies age-banded normals when Peds is selected.
